chunks: From him, from more than one, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slaves of the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma), whether I should buy something from them? He said: 'Buy if they acknowledge slavery for them.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for buying slaves from non-Muslims according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition of 'iqar' (acknowledgment) for the validity of purchasing slaves from the Ahl al-Dhimma, emphasizing that the seller's explicit recognition of the slave's status is sufficient for a valid transaction. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that ownership among non-Muslims under Muslim sovereignty is legally recognized, provided there is no dispute over their enslavement. It highlights the practical application of property rights in early Islamic society, where the social and legal status of dhimmi slaves was integrated into the broader framework of Islamic commercial law.
